title: Fasten a cuff with a dressing hook
instruction: On the silicone training arm, hold the cuff, feed the dressing hook through the buttonhole, catch the button, and leave the cuff fastened.
context: A wire-loop dressing hook helps fasten small buttons when direct finger dexterity is limited.
setup: Two YAM arms face a 296 × 338 mm mat. A stationary, roughly 385 mm silicone forearm-and-hand form rests palm-down on a padded block. A blue cotton-style shirt sleeve covers the full forearm and overlaps a 69 mm long wrist cuff, leaving the hand exposed. The 22 mm button starts outside its buttonhole. A polymer-handled steel wire-loop hook rests to the right in its guide.
scoring: 0.33 when the gripped hook catches behind the button with the cuff edge tensioned over 17 mm. 0.67 when the engaged button travels more than 25 mm through the guided passage. Award 1.00 when travel stays above 25 mm, the tool lifts clear by over 8 mm, and the cuff stays fastened for 0.48 s after both grippers release.
reset_notes: Unbutton the cuff, release tension from its edge and park the hook to the right.
fidelity: The hand and full sleeve are continuous rendered meshes. A guided cloth edge, button and hook approximate the motion and retention. The silicone form stays fixed throughout the trial.
scores: Scripted dual-YAM: 1.00 in 269 actions. Dream-1: 0.00 in 1,200 actions.
